source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed electrical appliance safety checks

1. Start with the test records.
2.
completion:
2. Identify the appliance name, type, make, model, and serial number: Ensure that the failed safety check documentation includes the specific details of the appliance that was tested. This will help in identifying the appliance in case of future references or manufacturer recalls.

3. Record the date and time of the safety check: Accuracy is key; include the precise date and time the safety inspection was conducted. This detail will be important if any follow-up investigations or audits are performed.

4. List the safety standards and regulations used during the inspection: Document which specific safety standards and regulations were used to evaluate the appliance. This may include National Electrical Code (NEC) regulations, local codes, or other applicable standards.

5. Describe the procedure and test method used: Explain in detail the steps and methods that were employed during the safety check. This will help in understanding what parts of the appliance were tested and how the defects were identified.

6. Document the specific faults identified
